title: RETURNING AN ITEM TO THE STORE
conversation: Paul: Hi, I bought this camera here yesterday, and it's not working. Tim: Did you charge the battery and put it in correctly? Paul: Yes. I followed the directions to the letter. Tim: Do you mind if I take a crack at it? Paul: Be my guest. Tim: I usually have the magic touch . . . Hmmm, you're right. It doesn't work. Would you like a replacement? Paul: No, this is the second one I've had to return. I think I'll steer clear of this model. Tim: I hear what you're saying. It's frustrating when you get one bad unit, let alone, two! Paul: Yeah, it's a bummer! I'd like my money back. Tim: If you give me your receipt, I'll issue a credit to your credit card. But you might also try a different model or brand. Paul: Maybe I will try a different camera. Tim: We've got an excellent Canon camera that's the same price as this one. It would be an even exchange. Paul: Okay, I'll take it. I hope this one works out. Tim: If you're not happy with it, don't hesitate to bring it back.

idioms.meaning_en: following instructions or rules exactly and precisely
idioms.meaning_vi: làm theo đúng từng li từng tí, tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt
idioms.example: He followed the recipe to the letter, so the cake turned out perfectly.
idioms.context: Yes. I followed the directions to the letter.
idioms.fill_sentence: When baking French macarons, you cannot afford to make any mistakes or guess the measurements. Chef An told his students to follow the recipe to the letter, weighing every gram of flour and matching the oven temperature exactly. By obeying every written detail of the instructions, their pastries turned out perfectly.

idioms.meaning_en: to try to do something, especially something you have not done before
idioms.example: I've never fixed a car before, but I'll take a crack at it.
idioms.context: Do you mind if I take a crack at it?
idioms.fill_sentence: I have never baked anything in my life, as I usually just buy store-bought desserts. However, my sister's birthday is tomorrow, and she loves homemade treats. Armed with a detailed recipe, I decided to take a crack at making a complicated three-tier chocolate cake from scratch.

idioms.meaning_en: please go ahead; try it yourself
idioms.meaning_vi: cứ tự nhiên, xin cứ việc
idioms.example: If you want to use my phone, be my guest.
idioms.fill_sentence: You think my grandmother's traditional beef pho recipe looks easy to cook? Be my guest; the kitchen is all yours and the apron is hanging by the door. Just don't blame me if the broth doesn't taste quite right on your first attempt!

idioms.meaning_en: to have a special ability to make something successful or work well; be very good at doing something difficult
idioms.meaning_vi: có biệt tài làm mọi việc suôn sẻ; rất giỏi trong việc làm những việc khó
idioms.example: Everything she plants grows well; she really has the magic touch in the garden.
idioms.context: I usually have the magic touch . . .
idioms.fill_sentence: Whenever our office printer jams or the computers freeze, we always call Minh to fix them. He just taps the machine once, and it instantly starts working perfectly again. Our boss always laughs and says that some people just have the magic touch with technology.

idioms.meaning_en: to avoid someone or something because they are unpleasant or dangerous, usually due to a bad experience
idioms.meaning_vi: tránh xa ai/cái gì (thường vì có trải nghiệm không tốt)
idioms.example: You should steer clear of that neighborhood at night.
idioms.context: I think I'll steer clear of this model.
idioms.fill_sentence: When riding your motorbike through the flooded streets of Saigon, navigating around deep potholes is crucial for your safety. To keep your vehicle undamaged and avoid getting stuck, you must steer clear of the heavily submerged areas near the canal.

idioms.meaning_en: to understand or empathize with someone's point of view
idioms.meaning_vi: Tôi hiểu những gì bạn đang nói / chia sẻ
idioms.example: I hear what you're saying about the price, but the quality is much better.
idioms.fill_sentence: I can hear the frustration in your voice, so please don't think I am ignoring your complaints. I hear what you're saying, and I completely agree that the workload is unfair.

idioms.meaning_en: used to emphasize that something is even more unlikely or impossible than the first thing mentioned
idioms.example: I can't afford a new bike, let alone a new car.
idioms.context: It's frustrating when you get one bad unit, let alone, two!
idioms.fill_sentence: After paying my university tuition fees this month, I barely have enough money to buy a cheap bowl of instant noodles, let alone eat out at a fancy restaurant. I will have to borrow some cash from my roommate just to survive until next week.

idioms.meaning_en: a situation that is disappointing, annoying, or unpleasant
idioms.meaning_vi: một sự thất vọng, điều đáng tiếc, điều xui xẻo
idioms.example: It's a real bummer that the concert was canceled because of rain.
idioms.fill_sentence: My weekend plans to go camping were completely ruined when a heavy storm hit our town. It was a huge bummer because we had already packed all our gear and bought the food. Now, we are stuck indoors watching the rain wash away our holiday.

idioms.meaning_en: to refund money back to a customer's account / to give money back to
idioms.meaning_vi: hoàn tiền, cấp một khoản tín dụng hoàn trả
idioms.example: The store will issue a credit to your account within five business days.
idioms.context: If you give me your receipt, I'll issue a credit to your credit card.
idioms.fill_sentence: I returned the defective shoes to the department store, but since I had lost the original paper receipt, they could not give me a cash refund. Instead, the friendly store manager offered to issue a credit to my membership account, allowing me to use that exact amount on my next purchase.

idioms.meaning_en: a trade of equal value; when you return something and take something else that costs the same price
idioms.meaning_vi: đổi ngang giá, đổi đồng giá
idioms.example: Since the two cameras cost the same, it was an even exchange.
idioms.context: It would be an even exchange.
idioms.fill_sentence: I bought a blue sweater for fifty dollars yesterday, but when I tried it on at home, it was too tight. I went back to the clothing store today to swap it for the exact same design in a larger size. Since both items cost the same amount, the cashier processed it as an even exchange without charging me any extra money.

idioms.meaning_en: to happen or develop in a satisfactory or successful way
idioms.meaning_vi: diễn ra tốt đẹp, có kết quả tốt
idioms.example: I hope your new job works out for you.
idioms.context: I hope this one works out.
idioms.fill_sentence: Our group had a terrible time scheduling the project meeting because everyone had different part-time jobs and classes. We finally decided to meet online at midnight, hoping this difficult plan would actually work out. Fortunately, everyone joined on time, we finished the slides quickly, and we got an A grade.

idioms.meaning_en: feel free to do something; do it without worrying or waiting
idioms.meaning_vi: đừng ngần ngại làm gì đó
idioms.example: If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to ask.
idioms.context: If you're not happy with it, don't hesitate to bring it back.
idioms.fill_sentence: As a new intern, you might feel shy about asking for help when you get stuck. However, please don't hesitate to contact me at any time of the day. I would much prefer you ask immediately rather than wasting hours worrying and waiting for the weekly meeting.
